entries.title: Technology goes green
entries.quote: 2007 may well see an escalation in the search for both genuine causes and scapegoats for climate change
entries.subject: Green IT
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Technology Part One, 18 January 2007). Rank is the order within that part. Quote truncated in the source text after 'scapegoats for'; completed from context.

entries.title: Reinventing the user interface
entries.quote: In 2007, companies that manage to minimize product complexity may achieve greater success than competitors with superior, but relatively inaccessible, technology.
entries.subject: User interface simplicity
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Technology Part One, 18 January 2007). Rank is the order within that part.

entries.title: Heeding the hidden costs of storage
entries.quote: However in 2007, consumers and businesses may start to worry about some of the various indirect costs of digital storage, rather than just celebrating its seemingly endless price deflation.
entries.subject: Digital storage costs
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Technology Part One, 18 January 2007). Rank is the order within that part.

entries.title: The business case for biometrics
entries.quote: But 2007 could see a major uptake in the adoption of biometrics for a large range of applications, driven by falling prices, the rising performance of key technologies
entries.subject: Biometric authentication
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Technology Part One, 18 January 2007). Rank is the order within that part.

entries.title: Analog apples and digital oranges
entries.quote: Headlines about new media's near vertical rise abound. Analyses of the travails of old media are similarly plentiful. Yet terms of reference often differ and context is sadly lacking. This causes misunderstandings that are likely to linger throughout 2007.
entries.subject: New media vs traditional media metrics
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication, Media report Part Two (18 January 2007). Part Two holds five sections; only the first heading was identified. Rank is the order within Part Two.

entries.title: The kilobyte is the killer application
entries.quote: Yet in 2007, much of the telecommunications industry focus is likely to remain towards high bandwidth applications based around large files ... and as a result, many operators may overlook a larger opportunity sitting right under their noses.
entries.subject: Low-bandwidth messaging services
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Telecommunications Part Two, 16 January 2007). Rank is the order within that part.

entries.title: The double-edged sword of triple play
entries.quote: 2007 is likely to see a raft of new triple and quadruple-play offerings taken to market, each backed by a very large marketing budget.
entries.subject: Triple-play bundles
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Telecommunications Part Two, 16 January 2007). Rank is the order within that part.

entries.title: The connectivity chasms deepen
entries.quote: In 2007, the gulf between these two groups is likely to deepen.
entries.subject: Broadband speeds
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Telecommunications Part Two, 16 January 2007). Rank is the order within that part. A 2015 edition chapter reuses the title 'The connectivity chasms deepen'.

entries.title: The rising cost of free telecommunications
entries.quote: PC-to-PC VoIP remains a marginal element of the world's voice traffic, and is likely to remain a small fragment of all traffic in 2007.
entries.subject: VoIP
entries.note: Secondary copy: Mondaq republication of the Deloitte report (Telecommunications Part Two, 16 January 2007). Rank is the order within that part.

notes: 6th edition by count from 2002. 'TMT Trends 2007' separate Technology, Media and Telecommunications reports, each republished on Mondaq in two parts. Read: Technology Part One (4 sections), Media Part Two (1 section identified of 5), Telecommunications Part Two (4 sections). Not read: Technology Part Two, Media Part One, Telecommunications Part One. The four unidentified Media Part Two sections cover media pricing, social networking monetization, video on demand to PCs, and virtual worlds.
